Well, I think here in Missouri as a whole, we're doing well. The pandemic is easing and I think that really has put some smiles back on people's faces. Kids, most generally speaking, are back at school. Most businesses are open. Some in the cities are still a little bit on lockdown. My district in particular, I think we're doing well. The biggest problem we probably have right now is employees. The $300 check that people get in addition to their unemployment is a disincentive to go back to work. And the stimulus checks are disincentives for people to go to work. And I'll give you a quick example. I've got a guy who's He's got a big construction guy, a big project going on right now in Illinois. And the day after the stimulus checks came out, he had 25% of his people not show up for work. So I think it goes to show the effect that these programs can have. People don't think they have an effect. What they do is significant. Employers right now are having a real problem trying to find employees because of this $300 check. I mean, it's $7.5 and a half to stay home on top of your unemployment shares that you're drawing. So a lot of people are staying home rather than go to work. Financially, they're better off. So it's hard to argue with that. I was told people as I was going through the process here, we need to find a way to incentivize people to work, not to incentivize them to stay home. And I think the process is backwards here from how we should have structured this. And as I was going through this, I lost the argument, obviously. But to me, it would have been a good way to go about this so that the employees would incentivize to go to work and the employers would have an employee then. And everybody was a win-win situation. But right now, this is the biggest problem we have as employers being able to find employees to be able to build their products and provide the products and services that they want to sell. And I think that's going to really dampen our economy's growth potential. I think our economy is still going to grow quite well over the next several months, but it could be even better if we had more people to work. and producing more products and providing more services. Because people are there wanting to buy these products at services, but not yet able to do it. A given example of supply chain, I think, is broken right now as a result of this. My refrigerator broke at my own personal home. It took six weeks to get apart for it. where they didn't have it on hand, but it took six weeks to get it. Those sort of things that are going to, I think, drag out the robust economy that we could have compared to, I think, what we will have. But the check runs out in September, so I think after that, the pandemic will be hopefully behind us by that time, and the check will go away, and people will be back to normal, and hopefully our economy will be back roaring like it was prior to the pandemic.
